content:
The market widely expects Apple to launch a new MacBook Pro with a touchscreen — the first ever Mac to support touch — by the end of this month, and Apple has long been preparing touch gesture functionality in macOS 27.2.

Apple today released macOS 27.2 beta 3 to developers, which includes several new code references related to upcoming touch interaction features. According to MacRumors' Aaron Perris, multiple built-in Apple apps have added a "gesture recognizer tool":

  • Photos added "PXGTouchDwellGestureRecognizer"
  • Notes added "ICTouchPressGestureRecognizer"
  • Safari added "touch sentinel recognizer"
  • Quick Look added "dragTouch functionality"

macOS 27.2 beta 3 also added a new long-press animation effect to the Dock, which may be another clue hinting at the upcoming touchscreen MacBook Pro:

Apple has long made multiple changes in macOS 27 to prepare for touchscreen support, including the addition of pull-to-refresh functionality for the first time. macOS 27 also added touch input support to Sidecar (the feature that lets you use your iPad as a second display for your Mac).

Bloomberg previously reported that Apple is optimising macOS for the upcoming touchscreen MacBook Pro. For example, when tapping a button or control, macOS will dynamically display relevant touch options; similarly, when tapping the menu bar, controls will automatically enlarge for easier touch operation.

In addition to the touchscreen, the new MacBook Pro is reportedly set to feature an OLED display and will be "noticeably lighter" than the current model.

The outside world expects Apple to unveil this new MacBook Pro by the end of this month (or should it be called MacBook Ultra?), though Bloomberg cautions that it could be delayed until November.
